quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which color is best to wear so others can see you?
questions.explanation: Wear orange, red, yellow, or green clothing on your motorcycle. These bright colors make you easier to see, day or night.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Let the front tire lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes smoothly and gradually. Do not lock up either tire. This gives you the shortest and safest stop.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. These signs tell you the traffic rules. Follow them.

questions.question: The best gear to wear when riding is:
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you. Use a DOT-approved helmet, eye or face protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Assume everything on your bike works properly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your bike completely before every ride.

questions.question: Alcohol starts to affect your abilities:

options.text: At about half the legal limit.

questions.explanation: One drink can affect your ability to ride safely. You can be impaired even below the legal limit. Do not drink and ride.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
Does not have a chin strap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. You can see as far as you need to ride safely.

questions.question: Before riding, check all of the following except:

options.text: Both brakes work and the brake light comes on.

questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire pressure and condition, oil and fluid levels, and all lights: headlight, taillight, signal lights, and brake light.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of an accident, you should:

options.text: Blend in with traffic and not be noticed.
Use turn signals only at night.
Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride close to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: Be visible to other drivers. Signal your moves, use your brake light, and keep proper lane position. Stay back from other vehicles, look ahead 12 seconds, and be ready for hazards.

questions.question: Keep a safe distance behind other vehicles to:

options.text: Have time and space to see and react to hazards.
Encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have time and space to see and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Keep a safe distance so you can stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also helps you see road hazards like potholes.

questions.question: What is the main substance in marijuana that affects the brain?
questions.explanation: THC is the main active substance in marijuana.

questions.question: What should you do with mirror checks?

options.text: Do them regularly as part of safe driving.
Avoid them because they distract you.
Avoid them because other drivers can see you.
Do them only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do them regularly as part of safe driving.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see what is behind you. This should be part of your normal driving routine.

questions.question: Which is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no cracks or loose padding.

questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet safety standards, fit snugly around your whole head, and have no cracks or loose parts. How it looks does not matter for safety.

questions.question: What is the danger of riding next to a car?

options.text: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
It is only dangerous on wet roads.
It makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot, and the car blocks your escape path.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed. Use both brakes when stopping and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: A front brake and a rear brake.
A front brake, a rear brake, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: A front brake and a rear brake.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: How can you help other drivers see you on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors, keep your headlight on at all times, and use your turn signals to help others see you.

questions.question: What happens if your motorcycle's chain or belt breaks?

options.text: The rear wheel suddenly gets more power.
The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly gets more power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
questions.explanation: If your chain or belt breaks, power to the rear wheel stops immediately.

questions.question: What should you consider when choosing a lane position?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which lane position makes your trip shorter.
Which position lets you pass more vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that allows other drivers to see you and gives you enough space to react safely.

questions.question: You have been drinking alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink of alcohol per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your body. Even one drink per hour can affect your ability to ride safely and your judgment.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe motorcycle riders should wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: Riding gloves are usually made of:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: Which is NOT a slippery surface?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane

questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, oil, and metal plates are all hazardous for motorcycles. Dry pavement is the safest surface.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, motorcycle riders should watch out for:

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking spot
Cars pulling out of parking spaces

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles, be careful. Cars may pull away from the curb or leave parking spaces without warning.
